why_trail.why: Verified directly (no crew dispatched -- LAUNCH_ORDER-2, admiral-post-568, explicitly forbids it for this attempt: the fix was already uncommitted in the tree). Diff inspected: exactly tests/test_spine_origin_isolation.py line 517, self.assertIn(str(self.foreign), message) -> self.assertIn(self.foreign.as_posix(), message), matching the stored-side pattern already at line 516. (a) chosen over (b) per LAUNCH_ORDER's judgment call: fixing the test's cwd-side assertion is correct because engine_cwd is always git's toplevel stdout, which git emits in posix form on every platform (including Windows) -- the message construction under test never needed changing, only the test's platform-naive assertion did. Two-platform argument: on POSIX, Path.as_posix() and str(Path) are byte-identical (no backslash to normalize), so Linux behavior is unchanged by construction; on Windows, self.foreign is a Path built from a Windows-style path, str() would render backslashes while the refusal message embeds the posix-form git toplevel string, so only as_posix() can match -- verified by reasoning, not by running Windows, which is unavailable here.

Independently reviewed by the commander (no reviewer crew dispatched -- LAUNCH_ORDER-2 forbids dispatch this attempt). Scope check: git diff shows exactly one line changed in tests/test_spine_origin_isolation.py; scripts/checklist_engine.py::origin_worktree_refusal and its main() call site untouched; test_it_is_pure unmodified.
